title: Uneven gains: the effects of elevated CO2 and temperatures on photosynthetic response of boreal tree seedlings
content: Since the industrial revolution, the concentration of carbon dioxide (CO2) in our atmosphere has increased by 50% due to anthropogenic activities, from 280 ppm in 1750 to over 420 ppm currently. This increase contributes heavily to global warming as CO2, a heat-trapping gas, enhances the greenhouse effect. Thus, the rise of CO2 and global air temperatures are concomitant and could have important effects on terrestrial ecosystems (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change 2023). These effects are expected to be particularly severe in higher latitudes ecosystems, such as boreal forests, since they are warming faster than other parts of the world (Sanderson et al. 2011). Indeed, observations of rising tree mortality rates at nearly 5% per year have been observed in boreal forests (Peng et al. 2011). As these ecosystems represent ∼30% of the world's total forest area, the direction of their response may severely impact primary productivity and global terrestrial carbon balance.
